stories.headline: Más de un tercio de estudiantes universitarios chinos presentan depresión
stories.finding: El meta‑análisis de 32 estudios, con 93 679 participantes, encontró que la prevalencia de depresión varió entre 12,1 % y 77,1 %, con una prevalencia global estimada del 34,70 %. Los resultados revelan una alta variabilidad y sugieren un aumento asociado a la pandemia de COVID‑19.
stories.takeaway: Este dato alerta sobre la magnitud del problema de salud mental en la población universitaria china, orientando a políticas de detección temprana y a la implementación de intervenciones preventivas en contextos académicos.
stories.paperTitle: Prevalence of depression among university students in China: a systematic review and meta-analysis
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Depression among university students in China represents a critical public health challenge, with emerging evidence suggesting exacerbated risks during the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite prior regional studies, a comprehensive national analysis comparing pre-pandemic and pandemic-era prevalence, while accounting for profession-specific stressors, remains lacking. This study aims to quantify depression prevalence across Chinese universities, identify high-risk subgroups, and assess the pandemic's impact. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted on PubMed, CNKI, Wang-fang Database, and Web of Science. The articles were cross-sectional studies focusing on the prevalence of depression among university students in China, with clearly defined criteria for diagnosing depression included. MetaXL 5.3 was used to pool the outcomes and perform a meta-analysis, assessing the prevalence of depression among university students and influential factors such as the impact of COVID-19. RESULTS: Data from 32 cross-sectional studies (n = 93,679) on depression prevalence among students were analyzed. The prevalence estimates ranged from 12.1% to 77.1%, with a summary prevalence of 34.70% after meta-analytic pooling. Subgroup investigations based on major, sample size, geographical region, gender, and the influence of COVID-19 were conducted. Prior to the pandemic, student depression prevalence was 35.0% (95%CI, 26.9%-43.4%), which increased to 38.7% (95%CI, 33.6%-44.0%) during and after the pandemic. DISCUSSION: This study underscores a substantial mental health burden among Chinese university students, intensified by pandemic-related disruptions. Medical students and those in high-stress regions warrant prioritized interventions. Systemic reforms in healthcare education and regionally tailored mental health policies are urgently needed. Longitudinal studies are critical to track post-pandemic recovery trajectories. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: CRD42024502949.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la atención plena frenar la rumiación?
stories.headline: Mindfulness mejora la regulación emocional y reduce la rumiación
stories.finding: Una revisión de estudios recientes muestra que los programas de mindfulness generan beneficios en la homeostasis psicofísica, la autorregulación emocional y las relaciones sociales. Estos efectos se observan en niños con discapacidades, sus padres y profesionales de la rehabilitación educativa.
stories.takeaway: Implica que integrar mindfulness en intervenciones de rehabilitación puede disminuir la rumiación y favorecer el bienestar de pacientes y cuidadores.
stories.paperTitle: Primjena mindfulnessa u području edukacijske rehabilitacije
stories.originalAbstract: Mindfulness (usredotočena svjesnost) se odnosi na proces usmjeravanja pažnje, odnosno svjesnost o onome što se događa u našem umu, tijelu i vanjskoj okolini u sadašnjem trenutku, sa stavom prihvaćanja, neprosuđivanja, prijateljstva i otvorenosti. Različita istraživanja iz područja medicine, psihologije, neuroznanosti i drugih srodnih disciplina ukazuju na to da provođenje mindfulness programa i tehnika može imati brojne dobrobiti kod različite populacije korisnika u području poticanja psihofizičke homeostaze, emocionalne samoregulacije i uspješnijih socijalnih odnosa. Na temelju ovih spoznaja definiran je cilj ovoga rada koji se odnosio na pregled i analizu rezultata dosadašnjih istraživanja u svrhu razmatranja načina i učinkovitosti primjene mindfulnessa u području edukacijske rehabilitacije, u sljedećim skupinama korisnika: 1) djeca s teškoćama u razvoju / osobe s invaliditetom, 2) roditelji, 3) stručnjaci uključeni u edukacijsko-rehabilitacijski proces. Rezultati recentnih istraživanja, obuhvaćenih pregledom literature u ovom radu, upućuju na pozitivne utjecaje mindfulnessa, na tjelesne, psihoemocionalne i socijalne dimenzije temeljene na promjenama u neurološkom i endokrinološkome statusu te aktivnostima autonomnog živčanog sustava. Promjene se također očituju u doživljaju sebe, kvaliteti međuljudskih odnosa, razini percipiranog stresa te usvojenim tehnikama i strategijama suočavanja s nepovoljnim životnim situacijama. Također, uočena je potreba provođenja daljnjih znanstvenih i primijenjenih istraživanja koja bi doprinijela brojnijoj i učinkovitijoj primjeni mindfulnessa u području edukacijske rehabilitacije.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la ACT aliviar la ansiedad en pacientes saudíes con depresión?
stories.headline: Ensayo aleatorizado muestra ACT como alternativa viable al cuidado estándar
stories.finding: Treinta y cuatro pacientes diagnosticados con depresión fueron asignados aleatoriamente a ACT (n=17) o a cuidados estándar (n=17). El estudio evaluó indicadores de ansiedad (GAD‑7, TMAS) junto a depresión y mindfulness, proporcionando evidencia empírica sobre la efectividad de ACT en este contexto.
stories.takeaway: Este diseño RCT aporta datos críticos para adaptar terapias basadas en mindfulness a poblaciones con alta estigmatización, orientando decisiones clínicas sobre intervenciones para la ansiedad y el estrés en contextos culturales similares.
stories.paperTitle: The Effectiveness of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) in patients presenting with Depression in Saudi Arabia
stories.journal: University Of Wales Trinity Saint David Research Repository (University of Wales Trinity Saint David)
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Depression continues to be a serious public mental health issue in Saudi Arabia. Cultural stigma, fewer resources, and reliance on medication limits access to evidence-based psychotherapies. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is a third-wave cognitive-behavioural intervention that promotes the use of mindfulness, psychological flexibility, and values-based living, which has potential for cultural adaptation. This thesis evaluated the efficacy of ACT through a systematic review and meta-analysis of the international literature, and an empirical clinical trial in Saudi Arabia. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis was undertaken in accordance with PRISMA; a comprehensive review of published randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of ACT for depression published from 2019 to 2024 was completed. The researcher also conducted a quantitative experimental study at King Khalid University Hospital. Thirty-four participants diagnosed with depression were randomised into either the ACT intervention group (n=17), or standard care control group (n=17). Psychological indicators of depression (BDI, PHQ-9), anxiety (GAD-7, TMAS), mindfulness (KIMS, MAAS), cognitive fusion (ATQ-F, ATQ-B), and thought suppression (WBSI) were measured three times: pre-intervention (T1), post-intervention (T2), and follow-up (T3). The data were analysed using repeated measure ANOVA, independent t-tests and regression models using SPSS v30. Results: The meta-analysis found ACT produced moderate levels of statistically significant reductions in depressive symptoms across various populations and delivery models. Additionally, the Saudi clinical trial demonstrated improvements in depression scores for ACT participants, specifically, BDI interventions decreased from 36.06 to 18.88, and PHQ-9 dropped from 17.71 to 8.65, contrasting with negligible change in controls. Improvements were seen in anxiety scores (GAD-7, TMAS) and negative thoughts (ATQ, WBSI), while mindfulness (KIMS, MAAS) was meaningfully better. Time × Group interactions were large and statistically significant, thus supporting ACT intervention versus standard care. Regression analyses showed group assignment was the strongest moderator of outcomes, while gender and age were of lesser importance. Improvements were deemed most beneficial immediately post-treatment and at follow-up, but regression to the mean was suspected on delayed assessments; thus, future booster sessions would be beneficial. Conclusion: This thesis provides converging findings from international trials, with a Saudi-based experiment that ACT represents an effective intervention that adapts for cultural resonance and acceptance for depression and related distress. ACT improves aspects of mindfulness, cognitive rigidity, and results in sustainable improvements to respondents' mental health. In Saudi Arabia, ACT therapy could be embedded into healthcare service provision through digital and scalable models to close treatment access barriers, reduce stigma, and offer a credible one-step improvement pathway. Long-term maintenance boosters are considered to convert the therapeutic gains to longer-term benefits.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la psicoeducación reducir el PTSD sin medicación?
stories.headline: La psicoeducación disminuye síntomas de PTSD en ensayos controlados
stories.finding: Una revisión sistemática incluyó 26 ensayos controlados aleatorizados con 3.304 adultos con PTSD. Nueve de esos ensayos mostraron reducciones significativas de los síntomas de PTSD tras intervenciones de psicoeducación, pese a la gran heterogeneidad de formatos y duración.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la psicoeducación, como componente breve y de bajo costo, puede ser una primera línea eficaz en la intervención del PTSD, orientando a clínicos a integrar formatos flexibles en la práctica cotidiana.
stories.paperTitle: Psychoeducation for posttraumatic stress disorder in adults: a systematic review of formats and delivery approaches
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a prevalent mental health condition that may develop following direct or indirect exposure to traumatic events. Psychoeducation offers a low-cost and accessible entry point to care. This review aimed to evaluate the effects of psychoeducation for PTSD and identify the conditions and delivery formats associated with greater effectiveness.Methods: We conducted a systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating psychoeducational interventions for PTSD in adults. Searches were performed in PubMed, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, PTSDpubs, and Cochrane databases, covering 1 January 2000 to 30 April 2024 with an additional targeted search for PTSD Coach trials conducted in July and August 2026. Eligible studies included adult participants and assessed psychoeducation delivered as either a stand-alone or primary component. Findings were synthesized narratively.Results: Twenty-six RCTs with a total of 3,304 participants met the inclusion criteria. Psychoeducational interventions varied substantially in format, duration, and delivery.Discussion: Nine trials demonstrated significant reductions in PTSD symptoms attributable to psychoeducation (one preventive intervention and eight post-diagnosis). All trials showing significant between-group effects used digital delivery, and most included form of human guidance. However, overall treatment effects were inconsistent across studies, and the methodological quality of the evidence was limited, with several positive trials presenting some concerns or a high risk of bias. Several trials also reported improvements in outcomes such as perceived stress, anxiety, stigma, and help-seeking intentions.Conclusion: Psychoeducation alone is insufficient as a stand-alone treatment for PTSD but remains a valuable component of stepped-care approaches. Future research should systematically assess outcomes such as stigma reduction and help-seeking behaviours, which are critical for engagement in intensive therapies. Preventive interventions may also benefit from focusing on high-risk populations identified through established risk factors, thereby enhancing trial design and minimizing the inclusion of individuals likely to remit without intervention.Registration: This review was not prospectively registered.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la variabilidad del ritmo cardíaco predecir trastornos mentales?
stories.headline: Baja variabilidad del ritmo cardíaco se asocia robustamente con la mayoría de los trastornos psicológicos
stories.finding: El meta‑análisis de 430 estudios (732 efectos, N = 62 264) mostró que la HRV en reposo es menor en la mayoría de los dominios de psicopatología, como esquizofrenia, trastorno bipolar, autismo, ansiedad generalizada, pánico, trastorno límite, TEPT y depresión mayor. No se observó asociación con TOC, ansiedad social ni trastorno de atención.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la HRV en reposo puede servir como biomarcador transdiagnóstico, facilitando la detección temprana y la monitorización del riesgo en pacientes con trauma y otros trastornos, lo que orienta intervenciones basadas en la regulación autonómica.
stories.paperTitle: A meta-analysis of heart rate variability and psychopathology: An investigation guided by the hierarchical taxonomy of psychopathology framework.
stories.journal: Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science
stories.originalAbstract: Although low resting heart rate variability (HRV) is associated with various forms of psychopathology, patterns of specificity and nonspecificity in the apparent transdiagnostic nature of resting HRV have not been systematically investigated. Existing research is dominated by disorder-specific studies, limiting conclusions about whether HRV reductions reflect mechanisms unique to particular diagnoses or a broader transdiagnostic vulnerability. Using the Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology framework, this Stage 2 Registered Report synthesized evidence from 430 studies and 732 effect sizes (N = 62,264) to quantify associations between resting HRV and psychopathology at multiple levels of specificity-from individual disorders to higher order spectra and superspectra. Across the hierarchy, lower resting HRV emerged as a robust correlate of most domains of psychopathology. For example, at the disorder level, lower resting HRV was significantly associated with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, autism, generalized anxiety, panic disorder, borderline personality, posttraumatic stress disorder, and major depression, but not with obsessive-compulsive disorder, social anxiety, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Psychotic conditions showed the strongest associations across all levels of the hierarchy, but sensitivity analyses indicated that these associations are likely influenced by study design and sample characteristics. Together with consistent moderator effects showing stronger HRV-psychopathology associations in samples with higher symptom severity, we conclude that decrements in resting HRV represent a transdiagnostic marker of systemic dysregulation reflecting illness severity rather than disorder-specific autonomic signatures. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influyen los apegos en nuestras defensas psicológicas?
stories.headline: Inseguridad del apego se vincula a defensas inmaduras, según revisión
stories.finding: Una revisión narrativa de veinte estudios empíricos encontró una asociación consistente entre estilos de apego inseguro y mayor empleo de mecanismos de defensa inmaduros, mientras que el apego seguro se relacionó con defensas más maduras. El apego ansioso mostró vínculos particulares con proyección, escisión y devaluación.
stories.takeaway: Este vínculo sugiere que evaluar el estilo de apego puede orientar la selección de intervenciones dirigidas a modificar defensas inmaduras, mejorando la eficacia terapéutica en adultos y adolescentes.
stories.paperTitle: The relationship between defense mechanisms and attachment: a narrative review
stories.journal: Research in Psychotherapy Psychopathology Process and Outcome
stories.originalAbstract: While a substantial number of studies investigate the nuances and clinical relevance of attachment styles and defense mechanisms separately, relatively few studies have explored the relationship between attachment styles and defense mechanisms. We aimed to provide a narrative review of empirical studies that used validated measures to assess the relationship between defense mechanisms and attachment styles in adolescents or adults. Twenty peer-reviewed studies published over the past 30 years were included. Except for one study involving high school students, all others focused on adults, mostly from community samples, with a few including clinical populations. Most studies employed various self-report questionnaires, though several used observer-rated or interview-based methods, with the majority using a cross-sectional design; a few studies used experimental and longitudinal designs as well. The studies' findings indicate an association between insecure attachment and greater use of immature defenses, while secure attachment is associated with more mature defenses. Anxious attachment was particularly linked to defenses such as projection, splitting, and devaluation, whereas avoidant attachment was associated with emotional suppression and denial. A subset of studies examined changes in these constructs during psychotherapy, suggesting that both defense mechanisms and attachment security may improve over time, and indicating the potential importance of reflective functioning as a mediator, as well as depressive immature defenses as obstacles to change. These results underscore the clinical relevance of assessing both attachment and defensive functioning and highlight the importance of addressing them as potential mechanisms of change in clinical contexts.

stories.headline: Alexitimia y rasgos autistas predicen dimensiones específicas de trastorno de personalidad
stories.finding: En una muestra de 89 personas con autismo, 51 con diagnóstico psiquiátrico distinto y 84 neurotípicas, los rasgos autistas predijeron la dimensión de trastorno de personalidad obsesivo‑compulsivo, mientras que los rasgos alexitimicos predijeron la dimensión borderline. Ambos tipos de rasgos también fueron predictores significativos de la dimensión esquizoide.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la evaluación de alexitimia y rasgos autistas puede orientar diagnósticos y tratamientos personalizados para trastornos de personalidad, facilitando intervenciones tempranas basadas en la regulación emocional y la cognición social.
stories.paperTitle: Alexithymic and autistic traits differentially predict personality disorder dimensions
stories.originalAbstract: Alexithymia and autism are variably characterized by social cognitive and perceptual deficits, which can lead to profound social interaction difficulties. Such difficulties are also the hallmark of personality disorders (PDs), but the potential link between alexithymia, autism, and PDs remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether autistic and/or alexithymic traits are associated with specific PD dimensions as measured by the Assessment of Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition (DSM-IV) Personality Disorders Questionnaire (ADP-IV). We included individuals with a formal autism diagnosis (AP, n = 89), individuals with a psychiatric diagnosis other than autism (NAP, n = 51), and neurotypical participants (NPs, n = 84). We applied linear regression analyses with autistic and alexithymic traits as predictors and PD dimensions as outcome variables, while controlling for age, depressive, and socially anxious symptoms. While autistic traits predicted the obsessive-compulsive PD dimension, alexithymic traits predicted the borderline PD dimension. Autistic and alexithymic traits were both significant predictors of the schizoid PD dimension. Taken together, our results point toward overlaps between autistic traits and specific PD dimensions that are well recognized as differential diagnoses of autism, while alexithymia was differentially linked to the borderline PD dimension.Lay abstractAutistic people have trouble identifying their own emotions and others' emotions. They also struggle to describe their emotions. People with alexithymia have similar difficulties. This can make it hard for autistic and alexithymic people to react appropriately to situations. Some may avoid places, while others may start overthinking. This can lead to patterns of behavior and thinking that limit us in our daily lives. If these patterns become a part of our personality, we may develop a personality disorder (PD). In our study, we looked at whether autistic and alexithymic people have certain PD dimensions. We included autistic participants, non-autistic participants with social-interactive difficulties, and non-autistic participants without social-interactive difficulties. We found that autistic features were linked to obsessive-compulsive PD dimension. Alexithymic features were linked to borderline PD dimension. Autistic and alexithymic features were linked to schizoid PD dimension. Our results point toward overlaps between autistic traits and PD dimensions that are well recognized as differential diagnoses of autism. The exception was borderline PD dimension, which was linked to alexithymic traits.

We applied linear regression analyses with autistic and alexithymic traits as predictors and PD dimensions as outcome variables, while controlling for age, depressive, and socially anxious symptoms. While autistic traits predicted the obsessive-compulsive PD dimension, alexithymic traits predicted the borderline PD dimension. Autistic and alexithymic traits were both significant predictors of the schizoid PD dimension. Taken together, our results point toward overlaps between autistic traits and specific PD dimensions that are well recognized as differential diagnoses of autism, while alexithymia was differentially linked to the borderline PD dimension.Lay abstractAutistic people have trouble identifying their own emotions and others' emotions. They also struggle to describe their emotions. People with alexithymia have similar difficulties. This can make it hard for autistic and alexithymic people to react appropriately to situations. Some may avoid places, while others may start overthinking. This can lead to patterns of behavior and thinking that limit us in our daily lives. If these patterns become a part of our personality, we may develop a personality disorder (PD). In our study, we looked at whether autistic and alexithymic people have certain PD dimensions. We included autistic participants, non-autistic participants with social-interactive difficulties, and non-autistic participants without social-interactive difficulties. We found that autistic features were linked to obsessive-compulsive PD dimension. Alexithymic features were linked to borderline PD dimension. Autistic and alexithymic features were linked to schizoid PD dimension. Our results point toward overlaps between autistic traits and PD dimensions that are well recognized as differential diagnoses of autism. The exception was borderline PD dimension, which was linked to alexithymic traits.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el sueño mejorar el rendimiento deportivo?
stories.headline: Sueño habitual se asocia bidireccionalmente con rendimiento físico y cognitivo en atletas
stories.finding: La revisión sistemática incorporó 68 estudios observacionales en atletas y personas activas, analizando el sueño nocturno habitual como exposición o resultado. Los hallazgos revelan asociaciones bidireccionales entre la duración/calidad del sueño y variables físicas, fisiológicas, cognitivas, psico‑perceptuales, de lesión y de competición.
stories.takeaway: Este dato subraya la importancia de monitorizar y optimizar el sueño en contextos deportivos, pues su mejora puede potenciar el rendimiento y reducir lesiones, ofreciendo una vía no farmacológica para la intervención clínica y la planificación del entrenamiento.
stories.paperTitle: Bidirectional Associations Between Habitual Nighttime Sleep and Physical, Physiological, Cognitive, Psycho-perceptual and Injury Outcomes in Athletes and Physically Active Individuals: A Systematic Review
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Sleep has been suggested as important for performance and wellbeing in physically active individuals through to athletes. Experimental sleep deprivation studies show that sleep loss can impair performance, but less is known about bidirectional associations between naturally occurring habitual sleep and performance-related outcomes in real-world settings. Objective: To systematically synthetise observational evidence on bidirectional associations between habitual sleep and performance-related outcomes in athletes and physically active individuals. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this review searched data from six electronic databases (PubMed, Web of Science, SPORTDiscus, ProQuest, CINAHL, and APA PsycINFO). Eligible studies included athletes or physically active individuals and reported associations between naturally occurring habitual nocturnal sleep and physical, physiological, cognitive, psycho-perceptual, injury and competition outcomes. Observational studies examining habitual nocturnal sleep as either an exposure or an outcome were eligible and were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Results: Sixty-eight observational studies were included. 52 studies examined sleep as an exposure, 23 examined sleep as an outcome, and seven examined associations in both directions. In sleep as an exposure direction, the most consistent evidence was observed for psycho-perceptual, competitive, and injury-related outcomes, with better sleep associated with more favourable mood, lower injury risk, and better competitive results. Physical outcomes showed more heterogeneous findings, with associations most apparent for explosive neuromuscular, sport-specific outcomes, while cognitive evidence was mainly related to reaction time, vigilance, and processing speed. In sleep as an outcome direction, psycho-perceptual factors, particularly fatigue, stress, tension, and anxiety were the most consistent predictors of subsequent sleep, while physical and physiological training load showed more variable, context-dependent associations. Conclusion: Habitual sleep is associated with performance-related outcomes, but the evidence supports a dynamic bidirectional relationship rather than a simple one-way pathway. Future research should use longitudinal repeated measures designs that assess sleep and performance simultaneously, alongside factors that may influence both

stories.headline: DMT‑harmine intensifica mindfulness y compasión en retiro meditativo
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 40 meditadores experimentados, la combinación de DMT y el inhibidor de monoaminooxidasa harmine incrementó significativamente los niveles de mindfulness, compasión, insight y trascendencia respecto al grupo placebo. Los efectos se observaron durante y al finalizar el retiro de tres días.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que los psicodélicos pueden servir como adyuvantes para profundizar prácticas de atención plena, abriendo nuevas vías terapéuticas en contextos de intervención basada en mindfulness.
stories.paperTitle: Meditating on psychedelics. A randomized placebo-controlled study of DMT and harmine in a mindfulness retreat
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: In recent years, both meditation and psychedelics have attracted rapidly increasing scientific interest. While the current state of evidence suggests the promising potential of psychedelics, such as psilocybin, to enhance meditative training, it remains equivocal whether these effects are specifically bound to psilocybin or if other classical psychedelics might show synergistic effects with meditation practice. One particularly promising candidate is N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT), an active ingredient of ayahuasca. AIM: This study aims to investigate the effect of the psychedelic substance DMT, combined with the monoamine oxidase inhibitor harmine (DMT-harmine), on meditative states, compared to meditation with a placebo. METHOD: Forty experienced meditators (18 females and 22 males) participated in a double-blind, placebo-controlled study over a 3-day meditation retreat, receiving either placebo or DMT-harmine. Participants' levels of mindfulness, compassion, insight, and transcendence were assessed before, during, and after the meditation group retreat, using psychometric questionnaires. RESULTS: Compared to meditation with a placebo, meditators who received DMT and harmine self-attributed greater levels of mystical-type experiences, non-dual awareness, and emotional breakthrough during the acute substance effects and, when corrected for baseline differences, greater psychological insight 1 day later. Mindfulness and compassion were not significantly different in the DMT-harmine group compared to placebo. At 1-month follow-up, the meditators who received DMT and harmine rated their experience as significantly more personally meaningful, spiritually significant, and well-being-enhancing than the meditators who received placebo. CONCLUSION: Investigating the impact of DMT-harmine on meditators in a naturalistic mindfulness group retreat, this placebo-controlled study highlights the specific effects of psychedelics during meditation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05780216.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el cuidado compasivo agota a los médicos?
stories.headline: El agotamiento compasivo altera la identidad profesional y creencias de los médicos
stories.finding: Una revisión sistemática de alcance analizó la literatura sobre fatigue compasivo, estrés traumático secundario y trauma vicario en médicos de especialidades adultas. Los autores hallaron que el fatigue compasivo no solo produce agotamiento emocional, sino que también perturba creencias fundamentales y la formación de la identidad profesional.
stories.takeaway: Comprender que el fatigue compasivo afecta la identidad profesional alerta a la necesidad de intervenciones que fortalezcan la resiliencia y el sentido de propósito, mejorando la salud mental de los médicos y la calidad de la atención al paciente.
stories.paperTitle: Understanding the cost of caring in medicine through personhood: A systematic scoping review of compassion fatigue, vicarious trauma and secondary traumatic stress
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Supporting seriously ill patients and their families through the illness trajectory renders physicians susceptible to compassion fatigue (CF). Traditionally characterized as emotional and physical exhaustion following sustained empathic engagement, emerging research suggests that CF involves deeper disruptions to belief systems and professional identity formation (PIF), alongside an interplay with other trauma-related strain including secondary traumatic stress (STS) and vicarious trauma (VT) within the broader 'cost of caring' framework. However, such conceptual understanding remains fragmented and poorly synthesized in physician populations. OBJECTIVES: This systematic scoping review (SSR) maps existing literature on CF, STS and VT among physicians in adult medical specialties, using the Ring Theory of Personhood to examine their defining features, exacerbating and mitigating factors, and existing interventions. METHODS: This SSR employed the modified Systematic Evidence-Based Approach that integrates human and AI-based resources. The research team systematically searched PubMed, Embase, PsycINFO, CINAHL and Google Scholar for articles published from 1st January 2000-30th June 2025, supplemented by searches on Elicit AI Pro. Eligible articles underwent content and thematic analyses, augmented by ChatGPT o3 Pro. RESULTS: Of 18,396 database abstracts and 497 Elicit AI Pro abstracts identified, 986 non-duplicate articles underwent full-text review, with 122 meeting the inclusion criteria. CF, STS and VT encompass moral, cognitive, relational and identity-related dimensions that shape belief systems and PIF. Sharing overlapping features, these constructs sit along a continuum, where early features of CF-including exhaustion, depersonalization and boundary erosion-may progress toward STS' characteristic post-traumatic stress-type intrusions. Unaddressed, these acute reactions can evolve into enduring cognitive and existential alterations denoting VT. This trajectory can be interrupted by individual and environmental protective factors. CONCLUSION: Reframing CF, STS and VT as a continuum of escalating strain disrupting physicians' PIF highlights the need for stage-specific interventions and effective assessment tools that better capture this expanded notion.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la escritura aliviar el burnout de los terapeutas?
stories.headline: Escritura expresiva aumenta la autocompasión y reduce el burnout en psicoterapeutas
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 67 psicoterapeutas, la escritura orientada a la autocompasión y la escritura libre redujeron significativamente el agotamiento emocional respecto al grupo control. Ambas intervenciones también incrementaron la autocompasión, según análisis de efectos mixtos y mediación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenciones breves y de bajo costo, basadas en la escritura, pueden fortalecer la autocompasión y mitigar el burnout, ofreciendo una herramienta práctica para la salud ocupacional de los profesionales de la salud mental.
stories.paperTitle: Effects of writing-based interventions on self-compassion and job burnout among psychotherapists: a three-arm randomized controlled trial and mediation analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Job burnout is an important concern affecting psychotherapists’ occupational health and professional sustainability. Given the emotionally demanding nature of psychotherapy practice, identifying feasible approaches to support psychotherapists’ self-care and occupational well-being is of considerable importance. This study aimed to examine the effects of writing-based interventions on psychotherapists’ self-compassion and job burnout outcomes, and to explore the potential indirect role of self-compassion in this association. A total of 67 psychotherapists were randomly assigned to a self-compassion-oriented expressive writing (SCO-EW) group, a free writing (FW) group, or a control group for a 6-week intervention. Self-compassion and job burnout were assessed at pre-test, post-test, and follow-up using the Self-Compassion Scale-Chinese Version and the Maslach Burnout Inventory-General Survey-Chinese Version. Linear mixed-effects models and mediation analyses were conducted. Writing interventions were associated with increased self-compassion and improved job burnout outcomes. Compared with the control group, both writing conditions showed greater reductions in emotional exhaustion, whereas SCO-EW also showed reductions in cynicism. However, SCO-EW and FW did not differ significantly across most post-test outcomes, whereas SCO-EW showed greater improvements than FW in self-compassion and overall job burnout outcomes from pre-test to the 1-month follow-up. Mediation analyses indicated that post-test self-compassion was associated with follow-up job burnout outcomes, with significant indirect effects observed for both writing conditions compared with the control condition. This study extends expressive writing research to the occupational health context of psychotherapists. Self-compassion-oriented expressive writing may represent a feasible approach to supporting psychotherapists’ occupational well-being, with self-compassion serving as a potential psychological pathway underlying these associations.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influyen intimidad y conflicto en la depresión?
stories.headline: Intimidad y conflicto predicen depresión a través de la satisfacción de pareja e identidad
stories.finding: En una muestra de 268 adultos emergentes italianos, la intimidad y el conflicto mostraron asociaciones con los síntomas depresivos. Estas relaciones fueron mediadas secuencialmente por la satisfacción de pareja y la satisfacción de identidad, y la satisfacción de identidad también medió la relación entre intimidad y depresión.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir en la satisfacción de pareja e identidad puede prevenir la aparición de depresión en jóvenes adultos, ofreciendo una guía práctica para terapias de pareja y programas de desarrollo personal.
stories.paperTitle: Conflict and Intimacy in Emerging Adults’ Romantic Relationships and Depressive Symptoms: The Mediating Role of Identity and Couple Satisfaction
stories.originalAbstract: Romantic relationships in emerging adulthood may be associated with depression, but the role of possible mediators of this relationship remains to be explored. The present study tested a serial mediation model where intimacy and conflict in romantic relationships were predictors of depressive symptoms through the mediation of couple satisfaction and identity satisfaction. The study was conducted on a sample of 268 Italian emerging adults, 60% female (Mage = 19, ds = 1.4), all involved in a heterosexual romantic relationship. The results showed that the association between intimacy and depressive symptoms was direct and sequentially mediated through couple satisfaction and identity satisfaction. A single mediation pathway through identity satisfaction alone also emerged. The association between conflict and depressive symptoms was direct and sequentially mediated through couple satisfaction and identity satisfaction. These findings suggest the importance of helping emerging adults develop appropriate skills in managing conflict and intimacy in romantic relationships as useful resources for identity satisfaction and depression prevention.

stories.hook: ¿Influye la apariencia en la evaluación de la psicopatía?
stories.headline: El sesgo estético distorsiona la valoración de la psicopatía
stories.finding: Una revisión integradora muestra que la estética facial, como la confiabilidad y atractivo, sesga la interpretación de rasgos psicopáticos, especialmente el criterio interpersonal-afectivo del Factor 1. El proceso dual indica que inferencias rápidas del Sistema 1 pueden ser reforzadas por el Sistema 2, manteniendo la distorsión en decisiones forenses.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo alerta a profesionales forenses sobre la vulnerabilidad de sus juicios a prejuicios visuales y justifica la adopción de protocolos de desenmascaramiento secuencial y justificación estructurada para preservar la objetividad clínica y legal.
stories.paperTitle: The Layered Architecture of Clinical Objectivity: How Aesthetic Bias Interacts with Structured Psychopathy Assessment
stories.originalAbstract: Psychopathy assessment, though methodologically rigorous, remains cognitively permeable to automatic perceptual inputs. This integrative review examines how aesthetic bias—specifically facial trustworthiness and attractiveness—shapes the interpretation of psychopathy-related traits and subsequent legal outcomes. We propose a sequential framework illustrating how bias propagates from neural appraisal to clinical interpretation and institutional consequence. Findings suggest that aesthetic bias operates as a probabilistic judgment shaper, primarily affecting the interpersonal-affective criteria of Factor 1. This process is explained through a dual-process account: rapid System 1 facial inferences form a perceptual anchor that System 2 deliberative reasoning may reinforce rather than correct. Consequently, subtle distortions in trait perception can cascade into high-stakes outcomes, including the severity of sentencing and danger classification. We conclude that implementing linear sequential unmasking and structured justification protocols is essential to safeguard the integrity of assessments. These procedural adjustments offer a robust framework for improving forensic objectivity.

stories.headline: Mindfulness reduce la adicción a videojuegos en adolescentes vietnamitas
stories.finding: En un estudio con 200 estudiantes de secundaria en Vietnam, la intervención de mindfulness mostró que múltiples constructos psicológicos asociados a la atención plena influyeron en la reducción de la adicción a videojuegos, mejorando el autocontrol, la regulación emocional y la atención.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo respalda la incorporación de programas de mindfulness en la prevención y tratamiento de la adicción a videojuegos, ofreciendo una intervención basada en evidencia que mejora la autorregulación y la salud mental de los adolescentes.
stories.paperTitle: The role of mindfulness in treating gaming addiction in high school students: A case study in Vietnam
stories.originalAbstract: The objective of this study is to understand how mindfulness heals gaming addiction among high schoolers in Vietnam by sampling 200 individuals. The analyses thus performed are robust enough to reveal that multiples of psychological constructs related to mindfulness can influence the reduction of self-control, alleviation, related stress, and further emotional control, social and emotional skills, enhancement of focus and attention, motivation for a healthier diet, and reduction of dopamine dependence. The present results also show that this holds the functioning of mindfulness as a significant mediator in healing from gaming addiction, with additional correlations found among constructs. In this study, the increased break was found to contribute more to self-control, emotional regulation, and attention enhancement. This analysis shows that the model is valid and reliable, such that mindfulness interventions tend to mainstreamably nudge adolescents toward engaging in better behaviors. This study points out the necessity of incorporating mindfulness training in the treatment of gaming addiction and promises insights relevant to educators, policymakers, and mental health professionals that will be beneficial in aiding youth in their digital-age challenges with gaming.

stories.headline: Casi 9 % de los dolientes chinos presentan duelo prolongado
stories.finding: Un meta‑análisis de 28 estudios con 10 994 participantes estimó que la prevalencia combinada de trastorno de duelo prolongado es del 8,9 % (IC 95 % 4,2‑17,6) y la de sus síntomas del 32,4 % (IC 95 % 18,2‑50,8). Estos datos revelan una variabilidad considerable y una carga significativa de síntomas de duelo en China.
stories.takeaway: Conocer la alta prevalencia de duelo prolongado y sus síntomas permite a profesionales de salud mental diseñar intervenciones tempranas y políticas públicas orientadas a la detección y tratamiento en la población china, reduciendo el sufrimiento y mejorando la resiliencia.
stories.paperTitle: Prevalence of prolonged grief disorder and its symptoms among bereaved individuals in China: a systematic review and meta‐analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Background: The prevalence of prolonged grief disorder (PGD) and its symptoms among the bereaved population in China vary considerably. Aims: This meta-analysis aims to estimate the prevalence of PGD and its symptoms among bereaved individuals in China. Methods: We conducted a literature search in major Chinese and English databases from their inception to 4 October 2023, for cross-sectional studies on the prevalence of PGD or its symptoms in bereaved Chinese individuals. The risk of bias of the included studies and certainty of the evidence were assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Studies Reporting Prevalence Data ('JBI checklist') and the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations (GRADE), respectively. The 'metaprop' package in R V.4.1.2 was used to synthesise the prevalence. Results: A total of 28 studies involving 10 994 bereaved individuals were included in the analysis, with JBI checklist scores between 3 and 7. The combined prevalence (95% confidence interval) of PGD and its symptoms was 8.9% (4.2% to 17.6%) and 32.4% (18.2% to 50.8%), respectively. PGD and its symptoms were most prevalent among those who had lost their only child (22.7%) and those bereaved by earthquakes (80.4%), respectively. The GRADE system assigned a very low certainty level to the evidence for the pooled prevalence of PGD and its symptoms. Conclusions: The pooled prevalence of PGD and its symptoms indicate a potential high need for grief counselling services among bereaved individuals in China. This need is particularly pronounced in those who have lost their only child and those bereaved due to earthquakes. Further methodologically rigorous studies are needed to provide more accurate prevalence estimates. PROSPERO registration number: CRD42023432553.

Further methodologically rigorous studies are needed to provide more accurate prevalence estimates. PROSPERO registration number: CRD42023432553.

stories.hook: ¿Pueden los movimientos oculares revelar el ADHD?
stories.headline: Duraciones de sacádos más largas distinguen a niños con ADHD en tareas de realidad virtual
stories.finding: En un estudio con 34 participantes con ADHD y 30 neurotípicos, los participantes con ADHD mostraron duraciones de sacádos significativamente más largas durante la tarea tradicional (Task 2). Esta diferencia se mantuvo tras ajustar por edad y sexo, ofreciendo una precisión discriminatoria modesta.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que los patrones oculomotores, especialmente la duración de sacádos, pueden servir como biomarcadores objetivos para identificar déficits atencionales en ADHD, facilitando diagnósticos más precisos y el desarrollo de intervenciones basadas en realidad virtual.
stories.paperTitle: Virtual Reality Attention Tasks in Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: II. Eye Movement Patterns and Multimodal Behavioural Integration
stories.originalAbstract: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder is associated with differences in behavioural regulation and oculomotor control.Previous studies have investigated eye-tracking measures to assess differences between people with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and neurotypical participants, but inconsistent results have been reported across tasks.This condition is increasingly being characterised as heterogeneous in nature, raising the possibility that multimodal approaches may better characterise it.Sixty-four participants (34 people with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and 30 neurotypical participants) were included.Participants completed ten virtual reality tasks in real-life contexts while background and behavioural performance (evaluated in Part I) and eye movement patterns (current study) were analysed.Oculomotor differences varied by task and the clearest difference was observed during the traditionally formatted task (Task 2) with longer saccade durations.After accounting for age and gender, saccade duration remained significant and had a modest discriminatory accuracy between groups.Combining oculomotor (saccade duration) with behavioural measure (omission error rate) in Task 2, improved classification performance.Likelihood ratio tests indicated that omission error rate significantly improved the saccade-duration-only model.Results suggest that combining behavioural and oculomotor measures can provide complementary classification information.Additionally, utilising ecologically valid tasks in virtual reality and multimodal integration may enhance objective assessment strategies for this condition.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo afecta la crianza positiva al ánimo adolescente durante la pandemia?
stories.headline: La crianza positiva protege contra la depresión adolescente en Corea
stories.finding: En una muestra nacional de 2 590 adolescentes coreanos, los síntomas depresivos se mantuvieron estables, la crianza positiva disminuyó y el tiempo compartido aumentó y luego cayó. Los análisis cruzados indicaron que la crianza positiva predijo menos síntomas depresivos posteriores, aunque no se confirmó en los modelos de intercepto aleatorio.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya que reforzar la crianza positiva puede prevenir la depresión en adolescentes, incluso cuando el tiempo familiar fluctúa, orientando políticas y programas de apoyo familiar en situaciones de crisis como la pandemia.
stories.paperTitle: Developmental processes linking depressive symptoms, positive parenting, and parent‐adolescent shared time across the pre‐ to post‐ COVID ‐19 pandemic periods among Korean adolescents
stories.originalAbstract: Previous research links adolescent depressive symptoms to positive parenting and parent-adolescent shared time. However, their longitudinal associations across the pandemic era remain less understood, particularly among Korean adolescents. This study examined longitudinal changes and prospective associations among these constructs across the pre-, during-, and post-pandemic periods. We used six waves of nationally representative data from the Korean Children and Youth Panel Survey (2018-2023; n = 2590; mean age = 12.99, SD = .13; range = 12-14; 45.8% girls). Repeated-measures analyses of variance examined longitudinal changes, while cross-lagged panel models (CLPMs) and random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) examined prospective associations. Results indicated that mean depressive symptom levels did not change significantly, whereas positive parenting generally decreased. Shared time increased through 2020 before declining. Positive parenting was prospectively associated with fewer subsequent depressive symptoms, with most corresponding cross-lagged associations significant in the CLPMs but not in the RI-CLPMs. In contrast, associations between parent-adolescent shared time and depressive symptoms varied across periods and models. Before the pandemic, shared time was associated with fewer subsequent depressive symptoms in the CLPM, whereas during the pandemic, the RI-CLPM indicated that greater-than-usual shared time was associated with higher-than-usual depressive symptoms at the subsequent assessment, suggesting a within-person risk-related association during the pandemic period. These findings reveal that associations between family dynamics and depressive symptoms vary across pandemic periods and models, informing family-based support during societal disruption.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo la ketamina revitaliza las mitocondrias astrogliales?
stories.headline: Ketamina de baja dosis reprograma mitocondrias astrogliales para antidepresivo
stories.finding: El artículo revisa evidencia que la ketamina de baja dosis actúa principalmente sobre la función mitocondrial de los astrocitos, más que mediante antagonismo del NMDAR. Este proceso implica la up‑regulación de adenosina, humanina y melatonina, precondicionando las mitocondrias astrogliales y generando la respuesta antidepresiva.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que los efectos antidepresivos rápidos de la ketamina pueden optimizarse enfocándose en la función mitocondrial astroglial, lo que abre la puerta a nuevos fármacos con menos efectos secundarios y a estrategias de precondicionamiento para trastornos del ánimo.
stories.paperTitle: Low Dose Ketamine Preconditions Astrocyte Mitochondria to Achieve Antidepressant Efficacy via Adenosine, Humanin, and Melatonin Upregulation and Efflux
stories.originalAbstract: Understanding the physiological changes induced by ketamine in mood disorders, while reducing its side effects, is likely to contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of the physiology underlying mood disorders, as well as to the development of faster-acting and more efficacious antidepressant treatments. An extensive review of the literature on ketamine and the pathophysiology of depression indicates that ketamine's antidepressant efficacy has classically been attributed to noncompetitive antagonism of the n-methyl-d-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) on the neuronal postsynaptic membrane, thereby reducing excessive Ca²⁺ influx through the NMDAR channel. However, recent evidence suggests that ketamine's antidepressant efficacy is mediated not by synaptic NMDAR antagonism but rather by its direct effects on mitochondrial function, arising from its amphiphilic structure. It is proposed that astrocyte mitochondria represent the primary target of ketamine, with the broader effects induced by ketamine occurring downstream of the optimization of astrocyte mitochondrial function and, consequently, astrocyte function. Developmental stress and trauma are proposed to differentially prime specific regions of the central nervous system, rendering them more susceptible to subsequent stressors through the epigenetic regulation of astrocytes. This process increases astrocyte reactivity and dysregulates astrocyte mitochondrial function in response to subsequent stressors, while also increasing blood-brain barrier permeability within these regions. At stress-vulnerable sites, ketamine may upregulate adenosine, humanin, and melatonin, thereby restoring astrocyte function and attenuating inflammatory activity within the local astrocytic microenvironment, including microglia, neurons, and oligodendrocytes. Ketamine's modulation of mitochondrial function is proposed to be mediated via NMDARs located on the inner mitochondrial membrane, leading to alterations in mitochondrial ionic regulation that enhance astrocyte mitochondrial resilience to stress, possibly through a preconditioning mechanism. Ketamine-induced increases in melatonin and humanin are proposed to suppress microglial activation, promote white matter remyelination, and restore neuronal activity, as well as patterned intercellular and interregional communication. This hypothesis-driven overview evaluates ketamine's capacity to restore astrocyte mitochondrial function and thereby counteract the consequences of developmental stress and trauma that underlie vulnerability to subsequent stress-induced depression.
